newsitem.title: PERU: Lima bolsa closes lower on foreigners' absence.
newsitem.headline: Lima bolsa closes lower on foreigners' absence.

text.p: Lima stocks fell moderately on Thursday for the fourth consecutive session on an absence of foreign investors, brokers said.
They forecast that the downward tendency will continue for a few more days, even though the low prices of local stocks should soon make the bolsa attractive again.

"We do not really know what is going on, but we think that foreign investors are concentrated in New York, which is more stable and where Peruvian stocks are cheaper," said Carlos Reyes, from Helvetia brokerage.
In Thursday's session, the General Index dropped 1.24 percent to 1,500.42 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.60 percent to 2,086.04.
During the session, a total of 29.43 million soles ($11.45 million) was traded in 1,536 operations. Of the 88 stocks traded, 36 fell, 33 remained flat and 19 increased.

According to Eduardo Rios, from Prisma brokerage house, the Peruvian stocks quoted in New York, such as Telefonica del Peru and Credicorp, were trading at a lower price there than in the local bolsa, which drew capital away from Lima.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted for 33 percent of the total volume with 1.8 million shares traded. It fell 2.15 percent to close at 5.46 soles.
Among other leaders, miner Atacocha achieved the largest increase and gained 1.84 percent to 0.54 soles with a total of 640,000 stocks traded.

Bluechips Credicorp and Telefonica were the only ones that had a significative fall. Credicorp fell 2.85 percent to $17.70, with 61,700 shares traded. The other leaders were off by levels of below one percent.
